stem.en: Imagine a stone with the same message in two scripts, and nobody today can read either of them. Would it help the way the Rosetta Stone did?

text.en: Yes, because any two scripts side by side are enough.

feedback.en: Two unknown scripts give nothing to start from. Scholars need one side they can already read.

text.en: No, because at least one of the scripts must already be readable.
Yes, if the stone is large enough.

feedback.en: More text helps only if part of it can be read. Size cannot replace a known script.

text.en: No, because only Greek can ever work as a key.

feedback.en: Greek worked because people still read it. Any language people still read could do the same job.

explanation.en: The Rosetta Stone worked because Greek could still be read. The known script gives the meaning, and the lost script can then be matched to it.

hints.en: What did the Greek part give scholars that the other parts could not?
